topics.label: Lecture introduction and objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture within the cancer course and states its learning objectives.

topics.label: Cancer evolution and the origins of genetic susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations arising in susceptible cells can support clonal evolution within a permissive microenvironment.

topics.label: Environmental contributions to cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the evidence that environmental exposures contribute to cancer rather than cancer being solely a matter of chance or inherited predisposition.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections can drive cancer, with Burkitt lymphoma providing a detailed example of interacting infectious causes.

topics.label: Mechanisms of carcinogen-induced DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental carcinogens produce DNA damage and mutations through mechanisms shaped by their chemical properties and biological processing.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish mutation-producing initiation from the promotional conditions that enable initiated cells to proliferate into tumours.

topics.label: Biological context and susceptibility to carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain and recap how the biological context of exposure influences the carcinogenic effects of an agent.

topics.label: Methods for identifying and assessing carcinogenic effects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the tools available for establishing carcinogenic effects and the limitations of the evidence those tools provide.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by summarising its conclusions and framing everyday exposure decisions as balances between risks and benefits.
